summary.text: 一 is a single horizontal stroke used for the numeral ‘one.’ An oracle-bone example records it in the phrase ‘one ox.’ The concrete source of the stroke—as a direct mark or one mediated by fingers or counting rods—remains unresolved.

formation.text: A one-stroke numeral graph for the abstract number one. It is classified as indicative, but the concrete route is unresolved: the line may have marked one directly or may have developed through counting with fingers or rods. This is a whole-graph analysis, not a compound of smaller parts.

history.text: The curated oracle-style and small-seal images each show a single horizontal stroke. They are modern redrawings of historical script styles, not artifact images, and do not establish a precise sequence of graphic changes.

The received Shuowen account gives 一 a cosmological role as the beginning from which heaven and earth are divided and the myriad things formed. This is a Han-era interpretation, not evidence that the graph depicted heaven or earth.

The dictionary labels 弌 an old form of 一. A proposed graphic derivation for 弌 is tentative, and no detailed transition from 弌 to 一 is established here. A separate study reports elaborated numeral spellings from the Spring and Warring States period onward, but the scan does not resolve every printed form to a distinct Unicode identity.

uncertainties.text: The cited oracle-bone inscription has no supplied date, and a sequence of forms across periods is not established here. The concrete source of the one-line mark—direct indication, fingers, or counting rods—also remains unresolved in the consulted analysis.
The numeral analysis is supported; the proposal that 一 originally depicted heaven or earth is not. The chronology and development of the current senses ‘a/an’ and ‘alone’ remain unresolved.

senses.period: Oracle-bone writing; exact date unresolved; additional senses attested in later cited textual sources
senses.text: An oracle-bone example uses 一 in the numeral phrase ‘one ox.’ The cited study describes the numeral as the smallest positive integer and discusses ordinal ‘first’ as well; these are attested uses, not proof of a hypothetical original meaning.
一 is also used with the present-day function “a, an.” Its date and development from the numeral sense are unresolved.
一 is also used with the present-day meaning “alone.” Its chronology and connection to the numeral sense are unresolved.

limitations.text: The oracle-bone example has no exact date. The 字源 account cites 玉篇 and 尚書 for beginning-of-number and ordinal uses, but the supplied evidence does not establish their chronology relative to the numeral attestation. Current records list ‘a/an’ and ‘alone’ without historical dating, so no semantic transition is asserted.
